rationale_brief: ci.note LIKE '%(producer)%' is the most selective filter; drive a single linear pass over cast_info (sorted by movie_id) and probe small dense-PK arrays for title.production_year and per-movie mc/cn check. rt and ct are structural (no predicates) — skip.

join_order.notes: t.id = ci.movie_id resolved by direct index since title is dense-PK
For mv, iterate mc[lo..hi); accept if cn_cc[mc.company_id[k]-1] == us_code. Memoize qualifier per mv to avoid repeat lookups (consecutive ci rows share mv since ci is sorted by movie_id).
Used only on surviving rows to materialize chn.name slice for MIN comparison.
No rt predicate — rt.id=ci.role_id is non-filtering for non-null role_id; skip entirely.
No ct predicate — ct.id=mc.company_type_id is non-filtering; skip.

data_structures.cn_country_code: mmap int16_t array, length 234997 (dense-PK lookup by company_id-1)
data_structures.title_production_year: mmap int32_t array, length 2528312 (dense-PK lookup by movie_id-1)
data_structures.movie_qualifier_cache: small LRU/last-mv memoization (since ci is sorted by movie_id, just remember last mv and its bool result)
data_structures.aggregation: two scalar slots: best_chn_name (string_view), best_title (string_view); compare lexicographically on update

parallelism.morsel_unit: cast_info row range (e.g., 256K rows per morsel)
parallelism.reduction: per-thread local (best_chn, best_title) merged at end via lexicographic min
parallelism.notes: Linear scan of 36M ci rows parallelizes cleanly; per-thread memoization of last mv qualifier is local.
